newsitem.title: USA: Stocks end lower with bonds on approach of election.
newsitem.headline: Stocks end lower with bonds on approach of election.

text.p: Blue-chip stocks closed lower Friday as the market reflected the nervousness of bond traders ahead of Tuesday's elections.
The Dow Jones industrial average ended down 7.45 points at 6,021.93. For the week, it was up 14.91 points.
In the broader market, declining issues led advances 1,229 to 1,147 on heavy volume of 463 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
"A lot of traders have stepped to the sidelines to see what the elections will bring," said Thom Brown, a managing director of Rutherford Brown & Catherwood.
"There's the fear of the Democrats carrying both houses of Congress and there might be a nervous reaction fearing a return of an inflationary scenario," he said.
In the bond market, the bellwether 30-year Treasury bond fell 14/32, raising its yield to 6.68 percent from 6.64 percent at Thursday's close.

The yield briefly slipped to a new 7-month low of 6.59 percent on news that the unemployment rate was unchanged at 5.2 percent in October, and job growth was at a moderate 210,000, which was in line with Wall Street expectations.
Two reports by private groups added to a picture of moderating economic activity.

A survey of the nation's purchasing managers showed that the manufacturing sector grew more slowly in October than in September. And a key forecasting gauge rose for the eighth straight month, though it was the smallest gain in that string of increases.

The National Association of Purchasing Management's prices index fell to 47.1 from 51.2 in September. The Conference Board reported that the Index of Leading Indicators, which is supposed to forecast economic trends six to nine months ahead, was barely up by 0.1 percent in September after a 0.2 percent increase in August.
The reports come just two days after the government said the economy slowed to a 2.2 percent rate of growth in the third quarter from a 4.7 percent rate in the second quarter.

"Virtually all the economic data we've seen this week suggests that at the Nov. 13 Federal Open Market Committee meeting, talk will begin on an easing," said Tom Carpenter, chief economist at ASB Capital Management Inc.
The Federal Reserve's policy-setting FOMC meets later this month to weigh monetary policy based on the most recent economic data.

The market will focus next week on Tuesday's elections. President Clinton's re-election has been largely anticipated, so Wall Street's worry has been that a Democratic sweep of the Congressional races may unsettle financial markets.
"I think we've got a bad case of pre-election nervousness setting in," said Brown. "People will wait and see if there are any surprises before making heavy commitments."

The stock of MCI Communications was in the spotlight on news that it was in merger talks with British Telecommunications, which has a 20 percent stake in MCI. MCI stock was halted at 27-1/4, up 1-7/8.
The news stoked buying in Sprint, which rose 4-1/2 to 43-3/4, and some regional Bells with Bell Atlantic up 1/4 to 60-1/2, Nynex up 1/2 to 45, PacTel up 1/8 to 34-1/8 and Ameritech, up 1/8 to 54-7/8.
Among other special situations, Inference Corp. lost 5-1/4 to 7 after the software producer warned that its third-quarter results would be below expectations.
Food Lion class A stock rose 9/16 to 9-1/8. The company said it would acquire Kash n' Karry for $26 a share in cash. Kash n' Karry rose 1-1/2 to 25-1/2.
Samsonite Luggage surged 3-3/16 to 36-15/16 after announcing a restructuring and plans to cut 450 positions Thursday.
The Nasdaq Composite index rose 0.27 of a point at 1,221.78. The Standard & Poor's composite index of 500 stocks fell 1.50 to 703.77. The American Stock Exchange index rose 3.86 to 572.58.
The NYSE Composite index of all listed common stocks fell 0.82 to 373.68. The average share was down 8 cents.
The Wilshire Associates Equity Index -- the market value of NYSE, American and Nasdaq issues -- was 6,841.787 down 9.543 or 0.14 percent.
